notes: Asserts the scenario's full arc on junie: ready -> working -> waiting -> working -> waiting -> working -> ready, where the two waiting episodes are raised by DIFFERENT TOOL CLASSES in one session -- the first by a mutating terminal command (`printf 'AFTER\n' > gate.txt`), the second by a READ-ONLY file open (`.env`, which ConfigFileDetector.isSecretFile puts behind HumanInLoop.shouldAllowAction inside OpenFileAgentAction). The read-only half is the whole point of the row; the mutating half is the path 2-19 already covers and is here only so one recording can tell the two classes apart. WHY THIS SHOULD PASS ON JUNIE (i.e. why it is NOT known_failing the way the claudecode sibling is): irrlicht has no hook channel for junie and therefore no tool-name allowlist to get wrong. The junie parser opens a permission on event.state=="INPUT_REQUIRED" plus the block's stepId, and its approval arm covers aeViewFiles and aeTool (the read-only block kinds) in the same case as aeTerminal/aeFileChanges/aeMcp -- so the class-blindness #1861 found missing in claudecode is structural here. The arc reaches waiting through TranscriptPermissionPending -> state_classifier.go:152 transcript_permission_prompt. PROVISIONAL: no junie recording exists (0 recordings, maturity=planned), so the daemon=full verdict is read off source plus the a2ux type hierarchy, and the one captured approval fixture is a TERMINAL approval. If the read-only approval turns out to ride a MessageBlockUpdatedEvent or TestRunBlockUpdatedEvent -- both approvable in a2ux, neither in the adapter's case list -- readonly_gate_waiting is the phase that fails and the cell becomes daemon=bug. The spec deliberately asserts the CORRECT behaviour either way and is not weakened. BIRTH SHAPE IS INFERRED, NOT OBSERVED: junie writes events.jsonl only when the first TASK starts (verified on disk -- two local session directories hold transcript.md and no events.jsonl), while the CommandPattern process matcher binds the junie process at launch, so a proc-<PID> presession is expected first and the real session is expected to appear already in `working` on its first line (a UserPromptEvent). Every post-birth phase anchors to the REAL session, never the presession row. record re-anchors if a recording shows otherwise. NO CYCLE COUNT is pinned beyond the two episodes the scenario itself asserts as its subject. OBSERVATIONS: tokens_nonzero only. cost is NOT asserted -- junie on the record host runs a local model through a LiteLLM proxy and the live LlmResponseMetadataEvent carries "cost": 0.0. model is left unpinned for record to fill from the recording; it is a property of the proxy's configuration, not of junie.

text: The proc-<PID> presession appears in ready once the junie process is matched at launch. junie has written no events.jsonl yet, so this row carries no transcript state.

The real session appears when the prompt creates ~/.junie/sessions/<session-id>/events.jsonl. Its FIRST line is a UserPromptEvent, so the real session is born already working -- birth and turn_start are one event for junie, deliberately not split into two phases.

Step 1's terminal command is gated: a TerminalBlockUpdatedEvent carrying approvalRequest arrives under event.state=INPUT_REQUIRED and the session goes working -> waiting. This is the half 2-19 already covers.
The user answers with Allow once; the same stepId is re-emitted under state IN_PROGRESS, which both resolves the permission and opens the tool. The command runs and the turn resumes -> working.

THE ASSERTION UNDER TEST. Step 2 opens .env, isSecretFile puts it behind shouldAllowAction, and the read-only approval must produce its OWN waiting episode -- not skipped, not merged into the mutating one. The block must be a ViewFiles or Tool block, not a second Terminal block; a second Terminal approval means junie shell-read the file and the run proves nothing (see the cell's vacuous-pass caveat).
The user answers the read dialog; the file is opened and the turn resumes -> working.
TaskState finalizes the task -> ready. The session does not remain waiting after the last dialog closes; TaskState additionally drains any prompt still held open.

Trailing idle: the session stays ready for >=10s after the last dialog, catching a session left pinned at, or falling back to, waiting. Junie replays its whole block set at task finalization (status COMPLETED, state COMPLETED); the parser must skip those long-resolved prompts rather than re-open them.
